decisions.rationale: Lead Sneasler and Froslass for immediate Fake Out pressure and the option to Mega Evolve into fast Snow Warning-boosted Blizzard offense. Kingambit provides strong defensive typing into Floette-Eternal and Sinistcha while punishing Incineroar's Intimidate with Defiant; Basculegion is the strongest late-game cleaner. Lycanroc and Scovillain offer less consistent value into the opponent's Water, Fighting, and Fire pressure.
decisions.notebook: Primary plan: use Sneasler's Fake Out to enable Mega Froslass pressure, preserve Kingambit for Floette-Eternal/Sinistcha and potential Intimidate exploitation, and conserve Basculegion as a late-game cleaner. Opposing Choice Scarf Basculegion may outspeed the entire team depending on investment, so scout or pressure it with Protect, Sucker Punch, and Thunderbolt rather than assuming Speed control.

decisions.rationale: Lead Sneasler + Incineroar: Intimidate crushes their physical core (Sneasler, Kingambit, Lycanroc, Basculegion) since they have no Intimidate of their own. Sneasler offers Fake Out disruption and CC for Lycanroc/Sneasler mirror. Back Kingambit (Defiant punishes any future Intimidate, Sucker Punch priority, Dark/Steel wall) and Sinistcha (Hospitality team healing extends games, Matcha Gotcha spreads on Water/Rock/Ground for their Basculegion/Lycanroc, Focus Sash survives hits). Skipping Floette-Eternal Mega and Scarf Basculegion: lose a Mega and a Scarf, but gain Defiant answer and party heal which better match this physically-heavy opposing squad.
decisions.notebook: Opponent has Sneasler/Kingambit/Basculegion mirrors (Adamant sets), Froslassite Timid Snow Warning Mega, Lycanroc-Dusk Focus Sash Tough Claws Accelerork priority, Scovillainite Bold Mega Spicy Spray. No Intimidate user on their side, so Incineroar Intimidate has free reign. Mega Froslass sets snow (boosts its own Ice SpD); modern snow does NOT boost Blizzard accuracy. Lycanroc-Dusk Adamant with max Tough Claws Accelerork is a major priority threat to plan around. Both Sneaslers have White Herb + Unburden for post-CC speed boost. Their Kingambit carries Life Orb (more burst than my BlackGlasses but loses the Dark-boost). Their Basculegion is Adamant Mystic Water (stronger Wave Crash but slower than my Jolly Scarf). Scovillain-Mega ability is Spicy Spray — treat as unknown debuff/buff effect, scout when possible.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out Incineroar prevents the guaranteed Flare Blitz OHKO into Froslass, while Mega Evolving establishes snow and Shadow Ball reliably pressures opposing Sneasler without Blizzard's spread penalty.

Fake Out opposing Sneasler to deny priority and possibly put it to sleep (only lose to a faster Sneasler Fake Out, which still leaves Incineroar online). Flare Blitz into Froslass for guaranteed 2x SE OHKO before it Megas and sets snow. Froslass is immune to my Sneasler's CC/Dire Claw and immune to Normal, so Flare Blitz is the only viable path to remove it. Even in the worst case (their Sneasler flinches mine), Froslass still goes down.
decisions.notebook: Opponent team: Sneasler (Adamant Unburden 252 Spe likely → 172 base / 344 Unburden), Froslass (Timid Froslassite → Snow Warning, 154-189 Mega Spe), Kingambit (Adamant Life Orb), Lycanroc-Dusk (Adamant Tough Claws Focus Sash → Accelerork priority threat to Incineroar), Basculegion (Adamant Mystic Water), Scovillain-Mega (Bold Spicy Spray). Mirror lead Sneasler + Froslass giving them faster Sneasler + faster Froslass vs my Sneasler + Incineroar. No Intimidate on their side; my Intimidate already dropped both opposing atks by 1. Modern snow does NOT boost Blizzard accuracy. Their Sneasler 140-172 base Spe; my Sneasler 157 — likely slower. Post-Unburden I'd be 314 vs their 280-344. Plan: Fake Out shuts down their Sneasler preferencing CC (denies Unburden trigger). Flare Blitz removes Froslass before it sets snow. Watch Lycanroc-Dusk Accelerork on Incineroar. Basculegion LastRespects/SurfAce needs Kingambit or Sinistcha to handle. Sneasler is Adamant Unburden; Sucker Punch from their Kingambit is a worry for my Sneasler next turn.

decisions.rationale: Close Combat pressures a likely KO on Incineroar before it moves, while Protect shields Froslass-Mega from the threatened super-effective Flare Blitz and also blocks Parting Shot. Sneasler remains fast enough to act first and can survive even a Helping Hand-boosted opposing Close Combat from the shown HP.
decisions.notebook: Primary plan: use Sneasler's Fake Out and Unburden speed to enable Mega Froslass pressure, preserve Kingambit for Floette-Eternal/Sinistcha and potential Intimidate exploitation, and conserve Basculegion as a late-game cleaner. Opposing Choice Scarf Basculegion may outspeed the entire team depending on investment, so scout or pressure it with Protect, Sucker Punch, and Thunderbolt rather than assuming Speed control. Opponent led Sneasler plus Incineroar in game 1.

decisions.rationale: Protect Sneasler from the faster opposing attacks while pivoting Incineroar into Kingambit. This avoids the guaranteed Close Combat KO on Incineroar and makes Kingambit the safer sacrificial target, while preserving Incineroar and Sneasler for the following turns.
decisions.notebook: Opponent roster and sets are known: Mega Froslass has Snow Warning, opposing Sneasler has Adamant Unburden with White Herb, and the back options include Life Orb Kingambit, Focus Sash Lycanroc-Dusk, Mystic Water Basculegion, and Mega Scovillain. Against Unburden Sneasler plus Mega Froslass, preserve Sneasler with Protect when Incineroar is threatened by Close Combat; use Kingambit as the safer Close Combat pivot, then pressure Mega Froslass while preserving Incineroar for later.

decisions.rationale: Pass and bring in Sinistcha: Hospitality restores its partner, Ghost typing blanks Close Combat, and Focus Sash with Rage Powder or super-effective Shadow Ball gives the safest counterplay while preserving Incineroar’s utility.
decisions.notebook: Against Unburden Sneasler and Mega Froslass, prioritize Sinistcha’s Hospitality, Rage Powder, and Fighting immunity to preserve Sneasler; retain Incineroar for later Intimidate or Parting Shot, and beware Defiant Kingambit when using Intimidate.

decisions.rationale: Dire Claw into Sinistcha breaks its Focus Sash before a perfectly accurate snow-boosted Blizzard; their combined minimum damage secures Sinistcha if it does not Protect, while Blizzard also pressures opposing Sneasler and bypasses Rage Powder redirection.
decisions.notebook: Primary plan: exploit Sneasler's Unburden Speed to enable Mega Froslass pressure, preserve Kingambit for Sinistcha or Floette-Eternal and potential Defiant value, and conserve Basculegion as a late-game cleaner. Opposing Choice Scarf Basculegion may outspeed the entire team depending on investment, so scout or pressure it with Protect, Sucker Punch, and Thunderbolt rather than assuming Speed control. Opponent led Sneasler plus Incineroar in game 1.

decisions.rationale: Rage Powder is critical this turn: it redirects Foe Sneasler's priority +3 Fake Out onto Sinistcha, who is Ghost-typed and immune to Normal, completely negating the Fake Out's flinch and damage and keeping my Sneasler free to act. With Sneasler unblocked, Close Combat into the Foe Sneasler mirror match deals ~50% (0.5x NVE) while the self -1 Def/-1 SpD triggers White Herb, which in turn activates Unburden for x2 Speed (157 → 314) for next turn — this finally lets my Sneasler potentially outrun the foe's Unburden Sneasler (280-344). Sinistcha's Focus Sash covers a Froslass Blizzard spread or Shadow Ball, and any damage to my Sneasler is acceptable risk given the 70% non-KO probability. Close Combat into Froslass is immune (Fighting on Ghost), Dire Claw into Froslass is only 12-27% and worse than pressuring the opposing threat, and skipping Rage Powder lets my Sneasler get flinched into a wasted turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 notes: Foe Sneasler ran Fake Out turn 1 (countered by my Sinistcha redirection immunity from turn 3 onward), Close Combat on Kingambit turn 2 (KO), and burned its White Herb so its Unburden is live. Foe has Kingambit (LifeOrb Defiant - hate Intimidate), Lycanroc-Dusk (Tough Claws Focus Sash), Basculegion (Adaptability Mystic Water), and Scovillain (Moody mega) backed up. Only 4 mons brought this game; 2 unrevealed. Sneasler self-debuffs (Close Combat) always preferred into foe Sneasler mirror to proc White Herb → Unburden. Sinistcha Ghost-typing is the key defensive pivot: Normal immune, Fighting immune; Rage Powder with Ghost-typed ally is the meta redirector. Hospitality restores Sneasler. Froslass-Mega Snow Warning keeps Snowscape up (boosting Ice-type SpD 1.5x). Protect back-to-back has steep penalty so don't chain. Incineroar must be saved for Intimidate or Parting Shot if Defiant Kingambit comes in. After Sneasler's Unburden procs, my 314 Speed narrowly edges min-foe-Sneasler 280; max-foe-Sneasler 344 still outspeeds.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Protect preserves Sneasler from the faster opposing Sneasler while snow-accurate Blizzard guarantees the opposing Sneasler KO if unprotected and also chips Incineroar. Even if Incineroar removes Froslass, healthy reserve Basculegion can finish Incineroar with a guaranteed Wave Crash KO.
decisions.notebook: Opposing Sneasler's Unburden Speed can exceed 314, so its exact Speed remains unresolved. Mega Froslass Blizzard is fully accurate in snow. Mystic Water Adaptability Basculegion Wave Crash is a guaranteed KO on this Incineroar even from 86% after Intimidate.

decisions.rationale: Sneasler Close Combat onto foe Sneasler (21% HP) is a guaranteed OHKO (42.8-85.2% range, both ends KO at 21%); the 0.5x resist still clears the 37-HP target with huge margin and removes the Sneasler mirror. Incineroar Flare Blitz onto Froslass-Mega at 2x SE rolls 57.6-111.7% for a possible OHKO — if it lands, Froslass faints before Blizzard and my Sneasler survives; if not, Sneasler still dies to the spread but I've traded one Pokémon for two active KOs. Dire Claw on Froslass is only 12-24% (waste); Fake Out is wasted since CC already OHKOs the flinched target. Trade the dying Sneasler for the most value possible.
decisions.notebook: Cross-game: White Herb cures on first stat drop only, then Unburden procs; subsequent self-drops from CC persist (relevant vs foe Sneasler Def/SpD stacking). Incineroar Fake Out is usable on its first action turn after switching in even if it was flinched previously. Sneasler CC at 0.5x vs Sneasler mirror still OHKOes 21% targets with 2x margin. Mega Froslass with -2 SpA still OHKOs 15% Sneasler in Snowscape via spread (Blizzard 44.9-102.6% min range); 14-20% on Incineroar with 0.5x resist. Foe game-1 bring = Sneasler + Froslass-Mega + 2 of {Kingambit (LO Defiant), Lycanroc-Dusk (Sash Tough Claws), Basculegion, Scovillain-Mega (Moody)}; Intimidate triggers Defiant on Kingambit so never Intimidate that switch-in. Lycanroc-Dusk Accelerock priority 2x Tough Claws OHKOes any Sneasler in slot 1. Sinistcha Ghost-typing is the only Normal/Fighting immunity redirector; Hospitality was the only healer. Future plan vs this foe: scout the unrevealed bench mons first turn after a faint; if Lycanroc-Dusk revealed, sacrifice Sneasler immediately to deny its Accelerock tempo, pivot Incineroar to Intimidate on entry; if Kingambit revealed, lead Incineroar + something that threatens Dark/Steel (Kingambit Defiant punishes Intimidate hard).

decisions.rationale: Close Combat plus Thunderbolt is guaranteed to KO Incineroar even at both minimum damage rolls, and both attackers move before it at equal priority.
decisions.notebook: Opposing Sneasler's Unburden Speed can exceed 314, so its exact Speed remains unresolved. Mega Froslass Blizzard is fully accurate in snow. Mystic Water Adaptability Basculegion Wave Crash is a guaranteed KO on Incineroar even from 86% after Intimidate. At -1 Attack, Sneasler Close Combat plus Mega Froslass Thunderbolt guarantees a KO on Incineroar from 69%.

decisions.rationale: Sneasler is fainted (slot 1 must pass). For Incineroar, I need to KO one opponent to convert to 1v1. Froslass-Mega is the bigger remaining SpA threat and has only 7% HP — Flare Blitz guarantees the KO with less overkill (57.6-111.7% range), meaning lower recoil (~19-37 HP) than Flare Blitz on the bulkier Sneasler (66.3-131.6% = ~22-44% recoil). After Froslass faints, Sneasler is alone at 21% with -1 Atk, -1 Def, -1 SpD — a manageable 1v1. Froslass's Blizzard only does 14-20% to Incineroar (spread 0.75x modifier, 0.5x resist, so it's not the main KO threat; Sneasler CC at -1 Atk does 67-96% and is the danger). If Sneasler uses Dire Claw instead (22.5-32%), Incineroar survives and I can win the 1v1. Parting Shot would not KO anyone and leaves me facing 1v2 — strictly worse.
decisions.notebook: Cross-game durable: White Herb cures on first stat drop only, then Unburden procs; subsequent self-drops persist. Sneasler CC at 0.5x vs mirror still threatens. Mega Froslass Blizzard spread is 14-20% on Incineroar (0.5x resist + 0.75x spread) — main Incineroar threat is Sneasler Close Combat (67-96% at -1 Atk), not Froslass Blizzard. When facing 1v2 with Incineroar as last mon, prioritize KO of the lower-HP opposing threat to minimize recoil and improve 1v1 odds; Sneasler with -1 Atk at 21% HP is more beatable in 1v1 than Froslass at 7% with full SpA. Foe game-1 bring was Sneasler + Froslass-Mega + 2 of {Kingambit LO Defiant, Lycanroc-Dusk Sash Tough Claws, Basculegion, Scovillain-Mega Moody}; scout unrevealed bench next turn. Never Intimidate a Kingambit switch-in (Defiant punishes). If Lycanroc-Dusk revealed, sacrifice Sneasler to deny Accelerock tempo.

reflections.summary: Won through clean piloting: Fake Out enabled Mega Froslass to pressure opposing Sneasler, Sneasler punished the Kingambit switch with Close Combat, and snow-accurate Blizzard removed Sinistcha and the weakened Sneasler before Close Combat finished Incineroar. The four-Pokémon preview plan was sound, and Mega Froslass was the correct Mega for immediate speed, snow, and spread pressure; Kingambit and Basculegion were not needed but remained appropriate backline options.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the same four and Mega Froslass option, but anticipate a Floette-Eternal or Choice Scarf Basculegion adaptation and preserve Kingambit specifically for Floette rather than exposing it to Sneasler's Close Combat.
reflections.notebook: Opposing Sneasler's Unburden Speed can exceed 314, so its exact Speed remains unresolved. Game 1 pattern was Sneasler/Incineroar lead with Kingambit/Sinistcha behind; Sinistcha supported Sneasler with Rage Powder. Mega Froslass Blizzard is fully accurate in snow. Mystic Water Adaptability Basculegion Wave Crash is a guaranteed KO on Incineroar from 86% after Intimidate. At -1 Attack, Sneasler Close Combat plus Mega Froslass Thunderbolt guarantees a KO on Incineroar from 69%. For game 2, preserve Kingambit against a possible Mega Floette adjustment and respect Choice Scarf Basculegion if it is brought.

reflections.summary: Lost primarily because Kingambit fainted on the turn it switched in (Turn 2) — Close Combat landed on the freshly entered slot and OHKOed it before it could act, handing opponent the Kingambit/Sneasler mirror for free. Sinistcha was then erased by Mega Froslass Blizzard in Snowscape on Turn 3, and despite Incineroar's super-effective Flare Blitz dropping Froslass to 7%, my own Sneasler fainted to incidental chip the same turn and Incineroar had no answer for opponent's Sneasler Close Combat on Turn 5. Team-preview also contributed: the four I brought (especially Sinistcha as the fourth) cannot function against opposing Mega Froslass — Grass/Ghost folds to Blizzard in Snowscape and brought nothing to threaten the Froslass lead, so the bring ceded the matchup before Turn 1. I had no Mega option, so opponent's Froslassite went uncontested.
reflections.adjustment: If a Froslass-Mega check is available on the full roster (e.g., a fast special attacker, a Choice user, or a steel/fire that doesn't fold to Blizzard), swap Sinistcha out of the four and bring it as a pivot option for Game 2. Open the same Sneasler+Froslass lead by clicking Close Combat into Froslass-Mega Turn 1 instead of Fake-Out mirroring — Froslass is the real win condition, not the opposing Sneasler. If Sinistcha must be brought, do not let it take a Froslass Blizzard alone; keep it behind a redirect partner or only commit it on predicted Protects. Never free-switch Kingambit into opposing Sneasler's Close Combat range again — verify a Protect or non-CC action before committing, or hard-switch in on a slow pivot turn.
reflections.notebook: Cross-game durable updates: Mega Froslass Blizzard in Snowscape OHKOes Sinistcha from full HP — any Grass/Ghost pivot is dead weight in this matchup, so the fourth slot must do something else. Opponent's Sneasler Fake Out turn 1 targets my Incineroar (support denial pattern), not my Sneasler — consider Fake-Out splitting or leading Incineroar in a slot that draws a less useful target. My Adamant Blackglasses Kingambit was OHKOed on switch-in by an opposing Sneasler Close Combat flagged as super-effective despite Fighting→Steel/Dark being 0.5x — possible simulator mis-flag, but treat my Kingambit as fragile to Sneasler CC on prediction reads and never bring it in raw. No Mega on my side means opponent's Froslassite is unopposed — every turn Snowscape is up compounds the problem. Future plans for Game 2: (1) if a non-Ice-vulnerable fourth exists on roster, drop Sinistcha from the bring; (2) lead Sneasler + Incineroar into the same opener and click CC at Froslass-Mega Turn 1 rather than mirroring Fake Out; (3) only pivot Kingambit in on turns opponent's Sneasler is locked into Protect, Parting Shot, or a non-CC move; (4) keep Sinistcha on the bench entirely if it is brought in next game unless a redirect partner can cover its Blizzard vulnerability.
